title: South Park pays homage to Star Wars with comical White House scene and fans label it 'perfection' - NewsBreak
text: South Park fans were left stunned as the animated sitcom slipped a clever Star Wars nod into the latest "unhinged" episode. During the Wednesday, August 20 South Park episode titled 'Sickofancy,' the character Randy Marsh is seen attempting to make a business deal with President Donald Trump. As he was projected into the Oval Office, Randy - who was creating a marijuana and tech company called Techridy - was in front of the president requesting a hefty investment in return for the sacrifice of Towelie. In this, the animated sitcom was clearly referencing an iconic scene in Star Wars: Return of the Jedi. South Park fans were in hysterics over the subtle nod as well as the clear jab at tech companies - namely Apple - for allegedly attempting to bribe the president with gifts. READ MORE: Fox and Friends host uneasy as Trump spills romantic detail live on air READ MORE: South Park's Karoline Leavitt joke in full - including brutal dig at her appearance In the scene, Randy said, "Greetings Mr. President, allow me to introduce myself. I am Randy Marsh from Integrity Solutions [snorts ketamine]. In order for our company to make 6 billion dollars we need you to reclassify marijuana on the national level." To which President Trump was seen cackling over the idea. Randy continued, "With your wisdom, I'm sure that we can work out an arrangement that will be mutually beneficial [snorts ketamine]. In return for your understanding, I wish to offer you a gift." Randy then returns to the character Towelie and said, "This wonderful towel." Towelie, alarmed that he was being used as a sacrifice, said, "Say what?!" Randy continued, "It is a luxurious towel made from the finest fabrics available and I'm sure it will - ahh I'm in a hole, ahh I'm in a hole." Randy's projection then abruptly zaps away. Trump then replies, Ok, put him in with the other gifts." As Towelie is swiftly taken away by Trump's team, he screams, "Wait, wait, there's been a misunderstanding." After the episode aired, South Park fans took to X, formerly Twitter, sharing their excitement over the sci-fi reference. One fan posted, "#SouthPark doing a #StarWars Return of the Jedi parody tonight was perfection." Another viewer added, "#SouthPark Randy really selling out Towelie in a clear homage to Return of the Jedi." While a third wrote, "I definitely wasn't expecting a Return of the Jedi reference. #SouthPark." New South Park episodes air every Wednesday at 10 p.m. ET on Comedy Central and is available for streaming the following day on Paramount+.
